terms.comment: The stress falls on the penult when it is long: quandō paenultima syllaba est longa, ut «amāmus» (Traupman 237); paenultima alone also serves. Lewis & Short calls paenultimus post-classical; Cicero says proxima ā postrēmā (Or. 217).

terms.gloss: the last but one, the penult
evidence: Cic. Or. 217 (Lewis & Short s.v. paenultimus, as proximus ā postrēmō)

phrases.latin: Quandō accentum in paenultimā syllabā pōnimus?
phrases.english: When do we place the stress on the penult?

sources: Lewis & Short: paenultimus · Lewis & Short: postremus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 237, p. 248.
